title: A farmhouse kitchen, Bunratty Folk Park
author: Joseph Mischyshyn, geograph.org.uk
caption: The kitchen of the Mountain Farmhouse at Bunratty Folk Park, rebuilt as a poor farmer's house from the Limerick–Kerry border: the kind of kitchen where the whole of Sive is played.

spots.label: The hearth
spots.note: The fire is the centre of the house. Every row, bargain and plea in the play happens in this one room.

spots.label: Pots and chairs
spots.note: A bare, poor house. Money is short, which is why Seán Dóta's money can buy Mena's agreement.

spots.label: The door
spots.note: Who comes through the door brings the outside world in: the matchmaker, the old suitor, the travelling men with their songs.

title: Sive is brought home
author: Sive, Druid's 2003 Irish tour: Ruth Bradley as Sive, with Barry Ward, Noel O'Donovan and Eamon Morrissey. Photo: Valerie O'Sullivan
caption: Liam carries in Sive's body: she has drowned in a bog hole.

spots.label: Sive
spots.note: Laid on the kitchen table, in the room where her life was bargained away.

spots.label: Liam
spots.note: The young man who loved her. He turns furiously on Mena.

title: A Kerry bog
author: Graham Horn, geograph.org.uk, 2008
caption: Turf cut by hand and stacked to dry, with dark water in the cut-away holes. The play's world is bog and mountain.

spots.label: Stacked turf
spots.note: Turf, cut each spring, was the fuel of every farmhouse: the hard, physical life of a small farm.

spots.label: A bog hole
spots.note: Water fills the holes in the bog. Sive runs out across the bog at night and drowns in a bog hole.

title: The Glavins' kitchen on stage
author: Sive at the Gaiety Theatre, Dublin, 2024, directed by Andrew Flynn; photo via No More Workhorse
caption: The whole play happens in this one kitchen. Behind its walls, a red sky over the bog.

spots.label: The table
spots.note: Where the match is made and where, at the end, Sive's body is laid.

spots.label: The sky
spots.note: The set puts the bog and the mountain right behind the house: the dark, open country Sive runs into.

title: Sive and Nanna
author: Sive at the Gaiety Theatre, Dublin, 2024, directed by Andrew Flynn; photo via No More Workhorse
caption: Nanna, Sive's grandmother, holds on to her: the one person in the house who takes her side.

spots.label: Sive
spots.note: Gentle, still a schoolgirl, with no say over her own life. Mena tells her:
spots.quote: You will have no name till you take a husband.

spots.label: Nanna
spots.note: Sharp-tongued with Mena, but she begs Mike to stop the match.

title: John B. Keane, 1983
author: Bernard Gotfryd, Library of Congress
caption: John B. Keane (1928–2002) ran a pub in Listowel, Co. Kerry. Sive, his first play, was put on by the Listowel Drama Group in 1959.

title: Othello Relating His Life Story to Desdemona
author: Henri-Jean-Baptiste Fradelle (1778–1865), Royal Shakespeare Theatre collection
caption: The story Othello tells the Senate in Act 1, Scene 3: at her father's house in Venice, Desdemona falls in love with him as he tells the story of his life.

spots.label: Othello
spots.note: He tells of battles, sieges, capture, slavery and escape. He wins Desdemona with words, not witchcraft, as Brabantio claims.
spots.quote: She loved me for the dangers I had passed, / And I loved her that she did pity them.

spots.label: Desdemona
spots.note: She chooses her own husband, against her father and against Venice's expectations: a bold act for a woman in her world.
spots.quote: She'd come again, and with a greedy ear / Devour up my discourse.

spots.label: Brabantio
spots.note: Her father welcomed Othello as a guest and a war hero, but not as a son-in-law. He later warns: she has deceived her father, and may deceive Othello.
spots.quote: Her father loved me, oft invited me

spots.label: Venice
spots.note: Rich, ordered and proud: Othello is its trusted general and still an outsider. Cultural context: power, race and a daughter's duty.

title: Iago watches
author: Othello (1995 film), directed by Oliver Parker, with Laurence Fishburne, Kenneth Branagh and Irène Jacob; still via TMDB
caption: Othello and Desdemona together, while Iago leans on a pillar and watches.

spots.label: Othello and Desdemona
spots.note: Their love at its height.
spots.quote: If it were now to die, / 'Twere now to be most happy

spots.label: Iago
spots.note: He vows to ruin their happiness.
spots.quote: O, you are well tuned now! But I'll set down the pegs that make this music

title: The Return of Othello (Act 2, Scene 1)
author: Thomas Stothard (1755–1834), for the Boydell Shakespeare Gallery
caption: Othello lands safely in Cyprus after the storm wrecks the Turkish fleet, and greets Desdemona. It is the happiest moment in the play.

spots.label: Othello
spots.note: In armour, a soldier back from the sea. His joy is so complete he fears nothing can match it again: a warning for the audience.
spots.quote: If it were now to die, / 'Twere now to be most happy

spots.label: Desdemona
spots.note: She has followed her husband to a war zone. He calls her his fair warrior.
spots.quote: O my fair warrior!

spots.label: The soldiers
spots.note: Cyprus is a military outpost: soldiers, weapons and men far from home. Gossip, drink and rank matter here (cultural context).

title: Othello's Tower, Famagusta, Cyprus
author: A.Savin (Wikimedia Commons), 2017
caption: A citadel in the walls of Famagusta, rebuilt by the Venetians, who ruled Cyprus from 1489 to 1571. Its nickname comes from the play, set in a Venetian fortress on Cyprus.

spots.label: The Lion of Saint Mark
spots.note: The winged lion carved over the tower is the symbol of Venice: the island belongs to Venice, and Othello governs it for Venice.

spots.label: The walls
spots.note: A fortress on the edge of the Venetian world, facing the Ottoman Turks. Once the Turks are drowned there is no enemy outside, so the war moves inside.

title: Othello and Iago
author: Othello (1995 film), directed by Oliver Parker, with Laurence Fishburne, Kenneth Branagh and Irène Jacob; still via TMDB
caption: Iago at Othello's ear: the temptation scene, Act 3, Scene 3.

spots.label: Othello
spots.note: He wants certainty and gets hints, pauses and pretended reluctance.
spots.quote: Give me the ocular proof

spots.label: Iago
spots.note: He warns against jealousy while planting it.
spots.quote: It is the green-eyed monster

title: G. V. Brooke as Othello and James Bennett as Iago, Act 3, Scene 3
author: Benjamin Holl, engraved from a daguerreotype; Yale Center for British Art
caption: The temptation scene on the Victorian stage: Othello turns on Iago and demands proof. Brooke was a Dublin-born actor famous in the role.

spots.label: Othello
spots.note: He seizes Iago. He wants certainty, and Iago gives him only hints, pauses and pretended reluctance.
spots.quote: Villain, be sure thou prove my love a whore; / Be sure of it; give me the ocular proof

spots.label: Iago
spots.note: He looks shocked and loyal, but every word is planned. He warns Othello against jealousy while planting it.
spots.quote: O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; / It is the green-eyed monster

spots.label: The caption
spots.note: The engraving prints a line from this scene, Othello's threat to Iago.
spots.quote: If thou dost slander her and torture me, / Never pray more

title: Desdemona (The Song of the Willow)
author: Théodore Chassériau (1819–1856), Metropolitan Museum of Art
caption: Act 4, Scene 3: preparing for bed as Othello ordered, Desdemona sings the willow song. Only Emilia is with her.

spots.label: Desdemona
spots.note: Quiet and sad, remembering her mother's maid Barbary, whose lover abandoned her. She still won't blame Othello.
spots.quote: Sing willow, willow, willow

spots.label: The harp
spots.note: The song is a story of a woman wronged by love: Desdemona's own story, though she can't see it yet.

spots.label: The lamp
spots.note: The light by her bed. In the next scene Othello enters with a light and says he will put it out, and hers.
spots.quote: Put out the light, and then put out the light

spots.label: Emilia
spots.note: She tells Desdemona that when wives go wrong it is their husbands' fault: the play's sharpest words about how men treat women.
spots.quote: But I do think it is their husbands' faults / If wives do fall

title: Othello and Desdemona
author: Alexandre-Marie Colin (1798–1875), 1829
caption: Act 5, Scene 2: Othello has smothered Desdemona. He believes he has done justice, not murder, until Emilia tells the truth.

spots.label: Othello
spots.note: His hand on his heart: the noble general destroyed. At the end he asks to be remembered as one who loved too much.
spots.quote: one that loved not wisely but too well

spots.label: Desdemona
spots.note: Reviving for a moment, she protects him even now and blames herself.
spots.quote: Nobody; I myself. Farewell.

spots.label: The white cloth
spots.note: A white cloth lies by her hand. Is the painter reminding us of the handkerchief, Iago's false 'proof'?

title: Desdemona
author: Othello (1995 film), directed by Oliver Parker, with Laurence Fishburne, Kenneth Branagh and Irène Jacob; still via TMDB
caption: Irène Jacob as Desdemona: brave enough to defy her father, loyal to Othello to the end.

spots.label: Desdemona
spots.note: Her last words protect the husband who killed her.
spots.quote: Nobody; I myself. Farewell.

title: Ira Aldridge as Othello
author: Henry Perronet Briggs (1791–1844), about 1830
caption: Ira Aldridge (1807–1867), an African American actor, was one of the first Black actors to play Othello, including in London in 1833, where some critics attacked him in racist terms.

spots.label: Ira Aldridge
spots.note: A reminder that race is at the heart of the play and of how it was staged: for centuries Othello was usually played by white actors.

title: The night of the murders
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: The opening: Andy, drunk, sits in his car outside the house where his wife is with her lover, loading a revolver.

spots.label: The revolver
spots.note: The film cuts between this night and his trial. Andy says he threw the gun in the river. The jury doesn't believe him: two life sentences.

title: The bus to Shawshank
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy arrives at Shawshank with the other new prisoners. (The prison is the real Ohio State Reformatory.)

spots.label: The bus
spots.note: New men arrive. Inside, the prisoners bet on which 'fresh fish' will crack first: Red bets on Andy.

spots.label: Shawshank
spots.note: Built like a fortress or a cathedral: a place made to show power.
spots.quote: I believe in two things: discipline and the Bible. Here you'll receive both.

title: The new arrivals
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy, still in his banker's suit, lined up with the other new men.

spots.label: Andy
spots.note: Calm and silent. That night one new man breaks down and is beaten to death by Hadley; next morning Andy asks his name.

spots.label: The new men
spots.note: Stripped of their clothes and names: from now on they are numbers.

title: Beer on the roof
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy's tax advice to Captain Hadley wins three beers each for the men tarring the roof.

spots.label: The beer
spots.note: A small reward, but for a moment they aren't prisoners. Andy sits apart and doesn't drink: he did it for them.
spots.quote: We sat and drank with the sun on our shoulders and felt like free men.

title: Brooks was here
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Brooks carves his name into the beam of his halfway-house room before he hangs himself.

spots.label: The carving
spots.note: After fifty years inside, Brooks can't live in the outside world: 'institutionalized'.
spots.quote: Brooks Hatlen was here

title: Mozart over the loudspeakers
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy locks himself in the office and plays Mozart to the whole prison. The men in the yard stand still.

spots.label: The loudspeaker
spots.note: Music fills the yard: the walls can't keep out beauty.

spots.label: The men
spots.note: Red says that for the briefest of moments every last man in Shawshank felt free.

title: Andy in the office
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy leans back as the record plays. He knows it will cost him two weeks in solitary.

spots.label: Andy
spots.note: Afterwards he says music is something inside you that they can't touch. Red warns him that hope is dangerous.

spots.label: The record player
spots.note: Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro: donated records for the library he built.

title: 'Get busy living'
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy and Red sit against the wall after Tommy's death. Andy tells Red about Zihuatanejo and the rock near Buxton.

spots.label: Andy
spots.note: He has chosen hope.
spots.quote: Get busy living, or get busy dying.

spots.label: Red
spots.note: Red fears the worst: Andy has asked for a length of rope.

title: The poster
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy's poster of Rita Hayworth, later replaced by others, hides what he's doing behind it for almost twenty years.

spots.label: The poster
spots.note: When the warden throws a stone at the last poster, it goes straight through: a tunnel.

spots.label: Andy
spots.note: Patience and time: he digs with a tiny rock hammer, a little every night.

title: The empty cell
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Norton looks into the tunnel behind the poster. Andy is gone.

spots.label: Norton
spots.note: The man who controlled everything is beaten by the prisoner he exploited.

title: Freedom in the rain
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Andy crawls through five hundred yards of sewer pipe and comes out into a creek in a thunderstorm.

spots.label: Andy
spots.note: Arms raised to the rain, as if washed clean. The film's most famous image of hope.

title: The warden's Bible
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: In Norton's safe: Andy's Bible, with the rock hammer's hiding place cut into its pages.

spots.label: The hollow
spots.note: Andy's note says it all.
spots.quote: Dear Warden, You were right. Salvation lay within.

title: Approved
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: After forty years, Red's parole is approved, once he stops telling the board what it wants to hear.

spots.label: The stamp
spots.note: Red says 'rehabilitated' is just a made-up word, and this time he's released.

spots.label: Red's photo
spots.note: Ellis Boyd Redding, prisoner 30265.

title: So was Red
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Red carves his own words beside Brooks's and breaks parole: he chooses hope, where Brooks gave up.

spots.label: The carving
spots.note: The same beam, two endings: Brooks's despair and Red's hope.
spots.quote: So was Red

title: Andy's letter
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: Under the black rock in the hayfield: money and a letter inviting Red to Mexico.

spots.label: The letter
spots.note: Andy kept his promise.
spots.quote: Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.

title: Zihuatanejo
author: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont; still via TMDB
caption: The last shot: Red walks along the beach to Andy, working on his boat. (Filmed at Sandy Point, St Croix.)

spots.label: The boat
spots.note: Andy, free, doing the thing he dreamed of.
spots.quote: I hope the Pacific is as blue as it has been in my dreams. I hope.

spots.label: The sea
spots.note: Open blue after decades of grey walls: the film ends in freedom and friendship.
spots.quote: They say it has no memory.

title: The Shawshank oak, near Lucas, Ohio
author: Tom Hart, 2013
caption: The white oak in the hayfield where Red finds Andy's box. A storm split it in half in 2011 (this photo is from 2013), and the rest fell in 2016.

spots.label: The oak
spots.note: Andy describes the place: a long rock wall with a big oak tree at the north end.
spots.quote: a rock that has no earthly business in a Maine hayfield

spots.label: The split trunk
spots.note: Under the black rock by the wall, Red finds money and a letter: Andy kept his promise, so Red keeps his and breaks parole.

title: The coal yard
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill Furlong at work: the coal and timber merchant who keeps the town warm.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: He worked his way up from nothing, the son of an unmarried mother. Now he has a business, a wife and five daughters to keep.

spots.label: The coal
spots.note: Hard, black, filthy work, and a living in hard times: 1985, businesses closing and people emigrating.

title: W. Furlong, New Ross
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill's lorry, with his name on it: everyone in the town knows him.

spots.label: His name
spots.note: Respectable and known by all, which is exactly what he risks at the end.

title: The boy on the road
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: On his rounds Bill sees the town's hardship: a young boy gathering sticks.

spots.label: The boy
spots.note: Mick Sinnott's son, out gathering sticks for the fire.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: He reaches out to the boy: one of the small kindnesses the title points to.

title: South Street, New Ross, 1993
author: Ben Brooksbank, geograph.org.uk
caption: New Ross, Co. Wexford, where the novella is set: eight years after its Christmas of 1985.

spots.label: The Tholsel
spots.note: The old town hall at the top of the street, with its clock: a small town where everybody knows everybody's business.

spots.label: The shops
spots.note: In 1985 businesses are closing and people are emigrating. Bill sees the hardship on his rounds and keeps his head down.

spots.label: People in the street
spots.note: When Bill walks home with Sarah, barefoot, people notice and look away.

title: At home
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill at the table with his family: the comfortable home he could lose.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: He has a good life, and he can't stop thinking about what he saw at the convent.

title: The girls at the convent
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Girls in grey shifts, barefoot in the cold, watched by a nun.

spots.label: The girls
spots.note: One of the girls in the chapel begs Bill to take her as far as the river.

spots.label: The nun
spots.note: The Church holds the power in the town. Nobody asks what happens behind the walls.

title: The ironing room, Gloucester Street laundry, Dublin
author: Old postcard, via Architecture of Dublin (Flickr)
caption: The ironing room of the Monastery of Our Lady of Charity of Refuge, Gloucester Street (now Sean McDermott Street), Dublin. It was the last Magdalene laundry in Ireland to close, in 1996.

spots.label: The women at work
spots.note: Women and girls washed and ironed here for no pay, some for most of their lives. The girls Bill meets at the convent are kept the same way.

spots.label: The crucifix
spots.note: The Church ran the laundries. In the novella the town knows what goes on at the convent and says nothing: the nuns have a hand in everything.

title: Eileen
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill tells Eileen what he saw. She says it has nothing to do with them.

spots.label: Eileen
spots.note: Practical and afraid for their girls: the nuns pay their bills, and their own daughters are well minded.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: He asks where he and his mother would have been if Mrs Wilson had thought that way.

title: The coal shed
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: On an early delivery Bill finds a girl locked all night in the freezing coal shed.

spots.label: The girl
spots.note: Sarah. She asks him to find out about her baby, who has been taken from her.

title: The Mother Superior
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Sister Mary (Emily Watson): smooth, polite and in control.

spots.label: Sister Mary
spots.note: She calls the night in the shed a game of hide and seek, mentions how scarce places at the school are, and hands Bill an envelope with money.

title: Brought in for tea
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: At the convent: Bill with the nuns and the girl, now washed and dressed. He leaves without asking about her baby.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: Silenced by politeness and fear for his daughters' places at the school.

spots.label: The girl
spots.note: Her name is Sarah, like Bill's mother's.

title: Mass
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: At Mass Bill stays in his seat at Communion.

spots.label: The altar
spots.note: The Church at the centre of the town's life. Bill can't go up: something in him has changed.

title: Taking Sarah
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill finds Sarah in the coal shed again and walks her, barefoot, through the town.

spots.label: Bill
spots.note: He decides not to bring her to the priest's house. He is doing the thing, not asking permission.

spots.label: Sarah
spots.note: Wrapped in his coat. People notice she isn't his daughter.

title: His own door
author: Small Things Like These (2024 film of the novella), directed by Tim Mielants, with Cillian Murphy; still via TMDB
caption: Bill comes to his own door with Sarah, afraid but hopeful. The novella ends before we see what Eileen or the town does.

spots.label: Bill and Sarah
spots.note: Happier than he has ever been, though he knows he will pay for it. The open ending leaves the reader to judge.

title: The Magdalene memorial seat, St Stephen's Green, Dublin
author: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin (Wikimedia Commons), 2015
caption: A bench in St Stephen's Green, Dublin, remembering the women who worked in the Magdalene laundries and the children born to some of them.

spots.label: The words
spots.note: Ireland now remembers what Bill's town wouldn't talk about. Keegan's novella is part of that remembering.
spots.quote: To the women who worked in the Magdalen laundry institutions and to the children born to some members of those communities – reflect here upon their lives.

title: Claire Keegan, 2007
author: Ian Oliver, at the Dublin Writers Festival
caption: Claire Keegan, from Co. Wicklow, published Small Things Like These in 2021. It was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.
